# Termivar v0.10.0-alpha.2

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Termivar v0.10.0-alpha.2 is an experimental prerelease. It is not
> production-ready and has not completed an independent security audit. Use it
> only on systems you own or are explicitly authorized to test.

> [!NOTE]
> **PREPARED RELEASE METADATA.** This checked-in note was prepared before
> publication. Its presence in source does not by itself establish that the
> tag, GitHub Release, downloadable archives, checksums, or attestations exist.
> The repository's GitHub Releases page is authoritative for availability.

## What this release is

Alpha.2 is a usability, reporting, and defensive-maintenance candidate for the
same bounded Termivar CLI introduced by alpha.1. It adds offline inspection of
saved assessment reports and makes the executable's compiled CLI surface
visible without running a scan. It does not expand the downloadable scanner's
feature composition or claim authority.

## Highlights

- `termivar report compare` reads two supported completed assessment JSON
  files and produces deterministic terminal, JSON, or standalone HTML
  comparison groups. One-sided observations are not labelled newly introduced
  vulnerabilities or verified remediation.
- `termivar scan --profile web-review --report-dir DIRECTORY` renders
  `assessment.html` and `assessment.json` from one completed in-memory
  assessment, then publishes `manifest.json` last with exact payload lengths
  and SHA-256 digests. The manifest is not a signature or attestation.
- `termivar report verify --dir DIRECTORY` checks the strict bundle layout,
  payload bytes, supported assessment schema, and declared summary without
  scanning, executing HTML, repairing files, or authenticating the producer.
- `termivar capabilities` reports build state, maturity, implementation state,
  and runtime prerequisites for the exact CLI feature gates compiled into that
  executable. It performs no runtime capability test and does not establish
  official build provenance.
- JSON and text diagnostics now retain typed, redacted OpenAPI and REST review
  audit outcomes so incomplete and ineligible reviews are distinguishable
  without exposing response bodies or sensitive values.
- Native OAST lifecycle, diagnostic accounting, and credential-input paths
  received bounded defensive maintenance. The separately recorded F3 active
  polling/verification issue remains unresolved.

## Included downloadable binary capabilities

When an alpha.2 release is published, its four native `termivar` archives use
the unchanged non-default `release-bundle`. In addition to ordinary bounded scanning,
reporting, and the offline commands above, it compiles exactly:

- the artifact adapter;
- normalization resilience;
- GraphQL review;
- OpenAPI review;
- REST read-only review; and
- resource authorization review.

Compilation does not activate an optional review. The bundle excludes
`ssrf-oast-review`, the standalone `termivar-oast` provider service, the legacy
scanner, the unsupported API listener, and the experimental proxy adapter.
The OAST correlation, provider, and SSRF review work present in the source tree
is auxiliary or opt-in source functionality, not a promised downloadable
alpha.2 CLI capability.

## Evidence and claim model

Observations remain distinct from vulnerabilities. Existing dispositions,
claim bases, stable capability identifiers, assessment schemas, digest domain
separators, exact-origin authority, and request ceilings are unchanged.
Comparisons preserve imported claims without endorsing them, and bundle
verification establishes only supported structure and consistency for the
bytes read. Neither checksums nor manifests establish source authenticity,
target authorization, safe HTML, scan correctness, or remediation.

## Upgrade from Venom

Alpha.1 already established the current `termivar` binary, `termivar-*`
package, and `termivar_*` crate identities. Alpha.2 adds no legacy `venom`
binary alias and requires no further product rename. Users coming from the
former Venom source epoch should still follow the documented migration guide;
historical and compatibility-sensitive Venom schema and digest identities
remain intentionally preserved.

When upgrading from alpha.1 after alpha.2 is actually published, replace the
verified executable rather than assuming identical behavior from the shared
`0.10.0` base. Alpha.1 does not contain `capabilities`, Report Compare,
`--report-dir`, or Report Bundle Verification.

## Installation and verification

Before GitHub publishes the tag and assets, there is no alpha.2 download. Do
not construct a download URL or treat a successful source build as a published
archive. Use the repository's Distribution guide and GitHub Releases page to
identify the release that actually exists.

When GitHub Releases shows `v0.10.0-alpha.2` published through the reviewed
create-once workflow, download exactly one archive for the intended platform
together with that release's `SHA256SUMS`. Verify the selected archive's
matching checksum, inspect its bounded single-executable layout, and then run:

```bash
termivar --version
termivar --help
termivar capabilities --format json
termivar report --help
```

The expected version is `termivar 0.10.0-alpha.2`. Checksum agreement is
byte-integrity evidence, not code signing or independent build attestation.
No crates, containers, installers, or package-manager channels are published
by this release workflow.

## Known limitations

- This remains experimental pre-1.0 software with unstable APIs, no production
  readiness claim, and no completed independent security audit.
- F3, the separately recorded active SSRF polling/verification defect, remains
  deferred and unresolved. `ssrf-oast-review` and its provider are excluded
  from the downloadable bundle.
- The scanner does not provide unrestricted crawling, browser-backed
  JavaScript execution, generic WAF bypass, arbitrary identifier mutation,
  broad REST fuzzing, or automatic vulnerability confirmation.
- Report comparison does not establish equivalent coverage, source
  authenticity, findings chronology, or remediation. Bundle verification does
  not prove that HTML semantically matches JSON or that either is safe to
  execute.
- Main-branch workflow archives are temporary candidate evidence. They are not
  tag-labelled release assets, published checksums, or tag-bound attestations.
